record_type_quote: The primary goal of this study was to replicate the watching eyes effect in a highpowered sample, adhering closely to previous methodology (i.e., [23]). Towards the latter goal, we sought to conduct a conceptual replication of Simpson and Willer (2008) [39] to investigate if SVO has different relationships with decisionmaking in public versus private conditions.

targets.title: Eye images increase generosity, but not for long: The limited effect of a false cue
targets.evidence_quote: The primary goal of this study was to replicate the watching eyes effect in a highpowered sample, adhering closely to previous methodology (i.e., [23]).
targets.outcome_quote: Given that our study used similar methodology as Sparks and Barclay (2013) [23], we can conclude that we failed to replicate the eyes effect in this study.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall failure verdict for the watching-eyes replication.

targets.title: Altruism and indirect reciprocity: The interaction of person and situation in prosocial behavior
targets.evidence_quote: Towards the latter goal, we sought to conduct a conceptual replication of Simpson and Willer (2008) [39] to investigate if SVO has different relationships with decisionmaking in public versus private conditions.
targets.outcome_quote: Notably, this analysis was underpowered and we cannot draw definitive conclusions whether SVO relates to responses to observation.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly say the SVO analysis was underpowered and cannot adjudicate the response-to-observation finding, despite some same-direction descriptive results.

reasoning: One new-sample experiment directly re-tests Sparks and Barclay and conceptually re-tests Simpson and Willer. Other watching-eyes and observation papers supply background rather than separately identified replication targets.
